propositions: CPython 3.12+ warns about deadlock risk when fork() is called in a multithreaded process, and the grounding harness hard-codes fork context on POSIX hosts
The default multiprocessing context must switch from fork to spawn to eliminate the deadlock warning while preserving cross-platform compatibility
Worker callables must be importable module-level names with pickleable arguments and return values; non-pickleable inputs or parent receive failures must return abstaining RunResult without raising

The public API must accept an optional caller-supplied multiprocessing context to support informed legacy/frozen-executable compatibility, with explicit fork selection placing thread-safety risk on the caller
One existing test fixture using an unpicklable local closure fails under spawn and must be replaced with a parent-only proxy while preserving crash-vs-timeout detection
The documented public contract must clarify importability and pickleability requirements and document the explicit fork escape hatch
